articles.title: ‘Australia has given me pathway, not a place in team’: Anaya Bangar on WBBL dream
articles.summary: Cricket News: Anaya Bangar's return to competitive cricket now has a potential timeline, with March 2027 set as the key date in her bid to pursue elite women's cric.
articles.body: Anaya Bangar's return to competitive cricket now has a potential timeline, with March 2027 set as the key date in her bid to pursue elite women's cricket in Australia and potentially earn a route into the Women's Big Bash League.The former Mumbai U-19 cricketer has been cleared by Cricket Australia to play community cricket and has been given a pathway to pursue elite women's cricket, subject to the governing body's eligibility requirements.Bangar, the daughter of former India cricketer and ex-India batting coach Sanjay Bangar, stressed that the clearance does not amount to selection for the WBBL or automatic entry into elite cricket. Instead, it gives her an opportunity to work towards that level.“I am preparing to return to women’s cricket in Australia with the aim of pursuing elite cricket from March 2027,” the 25-year-old said. “This has not been an automatic or an informal process. Cricket Australia has a framework designed to balance fairness, competitive integrity, and inclusion in women’s sport, and my case has been considered through that framework.”Bangar said she understands that she will have to earn any opportunity that comes her way.“Cricket Australia has given me a pathway, which does not mean that I have been given a place in a team. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.March 2027 eligibility checkpointBangar's immediate plan is to find a club and play community cricket in Australia as she works towards a return to the competitive game. Her participation in elite competitions, including the WBBL, will depend on Cricket Australia's Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.Under the policy, a player's serum testosterone concentration must remain below 10 nmol/L for at least 12 months to qualify for elite cricket.Bangar's eligibility will be assessed from March 2027, including through a required blood test.“My understanding from Cricket Australia's clearance is that my eligibility for elite women's cricket from March 2027 remains subject to the applicable policy requirements, including a blood test assessment at the same time. If that March 2027 test confirms that I continue to meet the required testosterone criteria, I will be eligible to pursue selection for elite women’s cricket, including the Women’s Big Bash League pathway,” Bangar said.Meeting those requirements would allow Bangar to seek selection, but would not guarantee her a place in an elite team.“I don’t expect my history or my identity to earn me a place on a cricket team. I want my cricket to earn me a place on a cricket team,” she said.Why Bangar approached Cricket AustraliaBangar had earlier sought clarity from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) over whether transgender athletes could compete in women's cricket in India. She said she received no response to a letter submitted last year.She subsequently approached Cricket Australia in June this year.According to Bangar, Cricket Australia assessed her medical records, blood tests, documents relating to her surgeries and a research report from Manchester Metropolitan University's Institute of Sport before reaching its decision.“After I published my athlete testing report and everything else, BCCI stayed quiet about it. Whereas Cricket Australia actually read my report, went through all my medical history and had a proper team assessing my case,” Bangar said.“I approached Cricket Australia and they gave me clearance to play in terms of fairness and inclusivity.”Bangar is now looking for a club in Australia, with community cricket set to be the first step in her attempt to rebuild her playing career and eventually pursue an opportunity in elite women's cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sonal Dinusha joins elite list of legends with remarkable run against India
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sonal Dinusha continued his impressive run against India by registering his fourth consecutive fifty-plus score in Test cricket on Thursday, putting h.
articles.body: Sonal Dinusha continued his impressive run against India by registering his fourth consecutive fifty-plus score in Test cricket on Thursday, putting his name alongside some of the game's most celebrated batters.The Sri Lankan left-hander reached the landmark during the final day of the second Test in Colombo, where his resilient innings helped the hosts keep their hopes of saving the match alive. Dinusha's latest half-century came after he had already produced three substantial scores across the two-Test series.𝟓𝟎-𝐩𝐥𝐮𝐬 𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚Douglas Jardine (ENG, 1932-1934)Everton Weekes (WI, 1948)Clyde Walcott (WI, 1948)Ken Barrington (ENG, 1959)Sonal Dinusha (SL, 2026)Dinusha began the series with a century and an 84 in the first Test. He then followed those efforts with 103 in the first innings of the second Test before completing another fifty-plus score in the second innings.The consistency has placed him in several notable statistical lists.Dinusha has become only the third Sri Lankan batter to record fifty-plus scores in all four innings of a two-Test series. He joins Kumar Sangakkara and Dimuth Karunaratne in achieving the feat.Sangakkara accomplished it against Bangladesh at home in 2013 and against England in England in 2014, while Karunaratne achieved the feat against South Africa at home in 2018.Dinusha's achievement against India is even rarer. He is only the second batter to score fifty-plus in each of his first four Test innings against India.The only previous batter to achieve that feat was Zimbabwe great Andy Flower during Zimbabwe's tour of India in 2000. Flower's scores across the four innings were 183*, 70, 55 and 232*.Dinusha has also entered another exclusive list involving India. He is the fifth batter to score fifty-plus in each of his first four Test innings against the country.England's Douglas Jardine achieved the feat between 1932 and 1934, while West Indies legends Everton Weekes and Clyde Walcott did so in 1948. England's Ken Barrington followed in 1959.Dinusha's latest contribution came at a crucial stage for Sri Lanka. His half-century, combined with a century partnership with Keshara Nuwantha, allowed the hosts to negotiate the first session of the final day without losing a wicket and maintain their hopes of securing a draw.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
